# Temple Scroll Column 7 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 7 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 7:4 — "yitshar chadash" — new oil terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "new oil" | Standard literal rendering of yitshar chadash |
| LOGOS | "new oil" | Same standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "freshly pressed oil" | Dynamic rendering emphasizing the fresh character |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET rendering "new oil." Parallel with "new wine" (tirosh) in Column 6 — consistency requires the same pattern. PNEUMA's "freshly pressed" adds production detail not in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 7:5 — "first fruits of oil" vs. "first portion of olive oil"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "first-fruits of-oil" | Hyphenated literal form |
| LOGOS | "first fruits of oil" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the first portion of the olive oil" | "Portion" for bikkurim; specifies "olive" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "first fruits of oil." "First fruits" (bikkurim) is the established term. PNEUMA's "olive oil" adds a specification not in the Hebrew (yitshar), which is a more general term for pressed oil.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 7:7 — "hin" — measurement term

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "half a hin of-oil" | Preserves Hebrew measure with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "half a hin of oil" | Preserves Hebrew measure, standard syntax |
| PNEUMA | "half a hin of oil" | All three agree on preserving the Hebrew unit here |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three translators agree. No resolution needed. The hin (~6 liters) is preserved as an ancient measure.

**Status:** Unanimous agreement.

---

## 7:9 — priestly anointing — verb choice

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "and-shall-anoint with-it" | Literal with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "and shall anoint with it" | Standard formal rendering of mashach |
| PNEUMA | "and use it to anoint" | Reordered for natural English flow |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "and shall anoint with it." Standard biblical phrasing for mashach. PNEUMA's reordering is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 4*
*Resolution: LOGOS 2, LOGOS/EMET 1, Unanimous 1, PNEUMA 0, Compromise 0*
